title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 46-48, the Longue Marche notes, c. Jan. 1981). Grothendieck has just observed that a morphism of 'models' V -> U over Q induces a morphism of etale (Galois) topoi B_V -> B_U over B_Q. Equivalently it induces an outer homomorphism of arithmetic fundamental groups E_V = pi_1(V) -> E_U = pi_1(U) over Gamma_Q. He now asks which such homomorphisms are geometric, and states a 'Conjecture fondamentale'.

Setting: V is a regular scheme of finite type over Q. U is an elementary anabelian variety over a finite extension of Q, i.e. an iterated fibration in hyperbolic curves. Take a morphism of etale topoi B_V -> B_U over B_Q, equivalently an outer homomorphism f: E_V -> E_U compatible with the outer maps to Gamma_Q. The following are conjectured equivalent:
(a) f comes, up to isomorphism (conjugation by the geometric group pi_U), from a morphism of schemes V -> U, which is then unique;
(b) f is 'anabelian': for every open subgroup H of E_V (written E_V^0 on the page), f(H) has trivial centralizer. The intended centralizer is the one in the geometric group pi_U = E_U^0, or in E_U.

The margin note says that for the statement one may assume only that V is a reduced variety and U elementary anabelian, with a remark on dimension.

On the next page Grothendieck checks necessity of (b) by reducing to V = Spec k, a point. There (b) becomes the 'conjecture préliminaire': for a k-rational point giving a section Gamma_k -> E_U, the induced action of Gamma_k on pi_U has no fixed points other than 1.

For V a point, (a) <=> (b) is a strong form of the section conjecture: every section with trivial centralizer is geometric. For dominant V -> U it is the Hom-form of the anabelian conjecture. Overall this is a single 'Hom-conjecture' covering both dominant and non-dominant (including constant) maps. The criterion distinguishing geometric homomorphisms is not openness of the image but triviality of centralizers of images of open subgroups.
errors: As stated, (b) => (a) seems false when U is not proper, e.g. an affine hyperbolic curve. Take a cuspidal (tangential) section Gamma_k -> D_x subset E_U at a point at infinity, and compose it with E_V -> Gamma_k. The resulting f satisfies (b): the centralizer of the image of an open subgroup of Gamma_k in pi_U is trivial, since the inertia part Zhat(1) has no Galois invariants and pi_U is centre-free. Yet f does not come from a morphism V -> U. Grothendieck accounts for such 'points at infinity' in the section conjecture of the 1983 Faltings letter; here they are not yet excluded. The same issue occurs for higher-dimensional elementary anabelian U, via boundary strata of a compactification.

The notation f|E_V^0 is ambiguous. If E_V^0 means the geometric fundamental group of V, then (b) fails for constant maps: the image is trivial and the centralizer is all of pi_U. This contradicts the next page, which treats the point case via sections. The coherent reading is that the condition concerns images of open subgroups of E_V, with centralizer taken in pi_U.

Uniqueness in (a) requires V geometrically reduced and connected, or a componentwise formulation. The hypotheses 'régulier' and 'variété' were being adjusted in the text and margin, showing the statement is not yet settled.

ideas.what: Hom-form anabelian conjecture: outer homomorphisms pi_1(V) -> pi_1(U) over Gamma_Q satisfying a nondegeneracy condition come from unique morphisms V -> U, for U elementary anabelian (iterated hyperbolic curve fibrations).
ideas.modern_name: Hom-form of Grothendieck's anabelian conjecture (relative/Hom version)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (letter to Faltings 1983, Esquisse 1984); proved for dominant maps to hyperbolic curves over sub-p-adic fields by Mochizuki (1999)
ideas.where_published: Letter to G. Faltings (27 June 1983); Esquisse d'un programme (1984), in less explicit form

ideas.what: Characterisation of geometric homomorphisms (dominant and non-dominant alike) by the condition that images of all open subgroups have trivial centralizer in the geometric fundamental group of U.
ideas.modern_name: centralizer-free / 'anabelian homomorphism' criterion; unified Hom + section conjecture
ideas.usually_credited_to: not standard; the literature uses 'open homomorphism' for the dominant case and treats sections separately

ideas.what: Necessary condition for the point case: for a rational point, Gamma_k has no nontrivial fixed points on pi_U (trivial centralizer of the image of a geometric section).
ideas.modern_name: triviality of Galois-invariants of the geometric fundamental group / centralizer of Galois sections
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore via weight arguments (Nakamura, Mochizuki, Hoshi and others) for hyperbolic curves over number fields

ideas.what: Equivalence between morphisms of etale topoi over B_Q and outer homomorphisms of profinite groups over Gamma_Q for K(pi,1) models.
ideas.modern_name: Galois categories / classifying topoi of profinite groups

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes a single criterion, triviality of centralizers of images of open subgroups, to characterise geometric outer homomorphisms. It is meant to cover both dominant maps and constant maps (sections) at once, instead of 'open image' plus a separate section conjecture. As literally stated it fails for cuspidal sections of non-proper U. A corrected version, e.g. with U replaced by a log or compactified object, or with cuspidal sections allowed in (a), would be a clean unified Hom-conjecture; it does not seem to be formulated this way in the literature.
missed.quote: b) f | E_V^0 est anabélien, i.e. l'image par f de tout sous-groupe ouvert de E_V^0 a un centralisateur réduit à 1
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The non-dominant Hom-conjecture is open and contains the section conjecture. An intrinsic group-theoretic criterion of this type could be tested in known cases, e.g. Mochizuki's sub-p-adic results or Hoshi's work on non-geometric sections. It also suggests looking for non-geometric homomorphisms with trivial centralizers beyond the cuspidal ones.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an early (1981) formulation of the Hom-form anabelian conjecture, two years before the Faltings letter. It has an unusual nondegeneracy criterion (trivial centralizers rather than open image) intended to cover non-dominant maps and sections together. It overlooks cuspidal sections, which he later addresses. The general programme is well known; the specific centralizer formulation is a notable unpublished detail.
